pool.text: William, Duke of Normandy, was crowned King of England in Westminster Abbey.
William II began building Westminster Hall, located near the abbey.
Edward I ordered the expulsion of the Jewish population from England.
The Hanseatic League established a trading base in the city.
Shakespeare constructed his Globe Theatre in the area of Southwark.
The Great Plague struck, killing a fifth of the population.
Odeon Cinemas, the largest cinema chain in the country, was founded.
The Austin Motor Company began manufacturing hackney carriages.
The record label EMI was formed in the city.
Victoria Coach Station opened as the city's main coach hub.
The red double-decker bus first appeared with the AEC Regent III RT.
The British Academy Film Awards have been held in London.
The Festival of Britain was held on the South Bank.
The Great Smog occurred and led to the Clean Air Act.
The BFI London Film Festival was founded and takes place every October.
Michael Bond created the refugee Paddington Bear character.
Jim Marshall founded Marshall Amplification as a guitar amp engineer.
Political boundaries were expanded and a new Greater London Council was created.
The Thames Barrier was completed to protect against tidal surges.
Three London Underground trains and a double-decker bus were bombed.
